questions.question: Which blood vessels carry pure blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulmonary Veins.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The veins that** carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart **are known as the** pulmonary veins.**
 
• The** four primary pulmonary veins—two from each lung**—that** empty into the left atrium of the heart** are the** largest** pulmonary veins. 
 
• The pulmonary veins are part of the** pulmonary circulation.**
 
• The main pulmonary vein**s receive blood from three or four feeding veins **in each lung, and drain into the left atrium.
 
• The** peripheral feeding veins** do not follow the **bronchial tree.**
 
• They run between the **pulmonary segments** from which they drain the blood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Cardiac vein:**

 
 
• The cardiac veins **returns deoxygenated blood **from the **myocardium to the right atrium.**
 
 
 
• **Pulmonary arteries:**
 
 
• These are blood vessels that **carry oxygen-poor blood from the right side of your heart to your lungs.**
 
 
 
• **Cardiac artery:**
 
 
• These are the arterial blood vessels of coronary circulation, which **transport oxygenated blood to the heart muscle.**

questions.question: What does the sum total of the population of the same kind of organisms known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Species.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__****

 
• The sum total of the populations of the same kind of organisms is called species.
 
• Species are often defined as a group of individuals with similar characteristics, where they can interbreed to produce fertile offsprings.

**Taxonomy**

 
• Taxonomy is the branch of biology that deals with naming, describing, and classification of all living organisms including plants. 
 
• Classification is based on behavioral, genetic, and biochemical variations.
 
• Organisms are classified into seven main categories: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species.
 
• The scientific classification of humans is as follows:
 
 
• **Kingdom: Animalia**
 
• **Phylum: Chordata**
 
• **Class: Mammalia**
 
• **Order: Primates**
 
• **Family: Hominidae**
 
• **Genus: Homo**
 
• **Species: Sapiens**

questions.question: Milk turns into curds faster in summer because

options.text: The growth of bacteria increases with the increase in temperature
The growth of bacteria increases with the decrease in temperature
The growth of bacteria decreases when the temperature remains normal
The temperature will have no effect on the growth of bacteria

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The growth of bacteria increases with the increase in temperature.**__

__
 
• Milk turns into curds faster in summer due to **the increase in the growth of bacteria with the rise in temperature.**
 
• High-temperature conditions are favourable for bacterial growth.
 
• Bacteria multiply faster in the **summer season.**
 
• Curd contains several microorganisms, the bacterium** Lactobacillus** promotes the formation of curd.
 
• Bacteria are also involved in the making of **cheese, pickles, **and many other food items.
 
• The use of oil and **vinegar** prevents spoilage of pickles because bacteria cannot live in such an environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The ideal temperature for curd formation is **37 - 45oC**, which is available in summer thus, it can be easily understood why milk turns into curd faster in summer as the temperature is higher in summer which promotes the bacterial growth

• Adding yeast to the bread-making process consumes carbon molecules and converts them to alcohol and carbon dioxide.
 
• Yeast reproduces quickly and emits carbon dioxide when it breathes.
 
• Gas bubbles flood the dough,** increasing its volume.**
 
• The employment of yeast in the baking business for manufacturing bread, pastries, and cakes is based on this principle.
 
• It is used to make food items like idli, dosa, bread, etc.

questions.question: Vitamin B Complex consists of how many vitamins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **The B complex consists of eight water-soluble vitamins that perform essential and closely related roles in the body's cellular function**__.
 
• These include thiamine (**vitamin B1**), riboflavin (**vitamin B2**), niacin (**vitamin B3**), pantothenic acid (**vitamin B5**), pyridoxine (**vitamin B6**), **biotin **(vitamin B7),** folic acid **(vitamin B9), and cobalamins (**vitamin B12**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• B vitamins play a vital role in maintaining good health and well-being. As the building blocks of a healthy body, B vitamins have a direct impact on your energy levels, **brain function, and cell metabolism**.
 
• B vitamins are especially important for women who are pregnant and breastfeeding. These vitamins aid in fetal brain development as well as reduce the risk of birth defects.
 
• And for expectant mothers, B vitamins may boost energy levels, ease nausea, and **lower the risk of developing preeclampsia**.
 
• B vitamins are thought to increase testosterone levels in men, which naturally decrease with age. They may also help men build muscle and increase strength. However, human studies confirming these claims are lacking. 
 
• Each member of the B-complex has a unique structure and performs unique functions in the human body.
 
• **Vitamins B1, B2, B3, and biotin participate in different aspects of energy production, vitamin B6 is essential for amino acid metabolism, and vitamin B12 and folic acid facilitate steps required for cell division.**

questions.question: Which one of the following will be resulted when an animal cell is surrounded by a medium with lower concentration of water?

options.text: No change in movement of water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Osmosis:**

 
• It is defined as the **movement of molecules of solvent **from a region of its **higher concentration to a region of its lower concentration **across a semi-permeable membrane.
 
• It is a passive process and happens without any expenditure of energy.
 
• It involves the movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration **until the concentrations become equal** on either side of the membrane.
 
 
• **An isotonic solution** is one that has the same concentration of solutes both inside and outside the cell.
 
• **A hypertonic solution** is one that has a higher solute concentration outside the cell than inside.
 
 
• If the** surrounding has a lower concentration of water **than the cell then w**ater will move by osmosis from the higher concentration (inside the cell) to the lower concentration **(outside the cell) and hence the **cell would lose water.**
 
 
 
• **A hypotonic solution** is one that has a higher solute concentration inside the cell than outside.

questions.question: In which organ of human body, are the lymphocyte cell formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Bone marrow.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Lymphocytes are primarily produced in the bone marrow, which is the spongy tissue inside some of your bones. These cells are an essential part of the immune system. After the initial formation, immature lymphocytes may travel to the thymus to mature into T lymphocytes, or stay in the bone marrow to become B lymphocytes.

The bone marrow is a primary lymphoid organ and a key player in the immune system as it is where the production and maturation of lymphocytes initiate.

There are two main types of lymphocytes: B lymphocytes (B cells) and T lymphocytes (T cells), each having different roles in the immune response:

__
 
• B lymphocytes (B cells) start and mature within the bone marrow. When these cells encounter a foreign substance (antigen), such as bacteria or a virus, they become activated and produce proteins called antibodies. Each B cell is programmed to make one specific antibody. These antibodies are designed to lock onto the surface of specific antigens to neutralize them and mark them for destruction by other immune cells.
 
• T lymphocytes (T cells) are formed in the bone marrow but migrate to the thymus (an organ located in the chest), to mature, hence the name T cells. T cells do not produce antibodies. Instead, they have different ways of recognizing antigens. Some T cells directly destroy the cells that carry certain antigens, while others help control the immune response.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liver:**

 
 
• The liver receives all the **blood** that exits the **intestines and stomach.**
 
• This blood is processed by the** liver**, which also breaks **down, balances, and produces nutrients.**
 
• It also **metabolizes medications** to make them more easily **absorbed by the body or nontoxic.**
 
 
 
• **Long bone:**
 
 
• Long bones are **tough, dense bones** that offer **stability, movement, and strength.**
 
 
 
• **Pancreas:**
 
 
• To digest food, the **pancreas produces pancreatic enzymes,** which are natural fluids.
 
• Ducts carry these **liquids via the pancreas**.
 
• They discharge into the **duodenum**, which is the top portion of the** small intestine.**

questions.question: Which of the following pigments causes the red colour in onions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anthocyanins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **red colour **of the **onion **is **due **to the **presence **of **anthocyanins **and **anthoxanthins **which belong to the class of **Flavonoids**.

 
 
• **Anthocyanins **impart **orange**, **yellow **or **purple colouration **while **anthoxanthins **impart **pale yellow **or **white **colour.
 
• These **pigments **are present in the **cell sap** and are **water-soluble**.
 
• The **inner epidermis** of** red onions** is **characteristically white**, **small **patches of cells sometimes redden, **containing **vacuolar **anthocyanin**.
 
• **Anthocyanins **are **flavonoid pigments **present in the **vacuoles **of **higher plant cells** that generate a wide diversity of colours ranging from orange and red to violet and blue.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carotenoids **are a class of more than** 750 naturally occurring pigments** synthesized by **plants**, **algae**, and **photosynthetic bacteria **

 
 
• These richly **coloured **molecules are the **sources **of the **yellow**, **orange**, and **red** colours of many plants.
 
• **Fruit and vegetables **provide most of the 40 to 50 carotenoids found in the human diet. 
 
 
 
• **Chlorophyll **is a **pigment **that gives **plants **their **green** **colour**.
 
 
• It also helps **plants create their food **through **photosynthesis**.
 
 
 
• **Betalains **are unique** nitrogen-containing pigments** found exclusively in **families **of the **Caryophyllales **order and some **higher-order fungi**, where they **replace anthocyanin** pigments.
 
 
• **Betalains**, **consisting **of **betacyanins **and **betaxanthins **are generally used as **colour additives **in food.

questions.question: Ozone layer is present in which layer of the Atmosphere?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Ozone** is a gas that is present naturally within Earth’s atmosphere. It is formed of **three oxygen atoms (O₃)**. It is much less stable than oxygen and is thus much more reactive, which means it can be more easily formed and broken down through interaction with other compounds.
 
• Ozone is mainly found in two regions of the Earth's atmosphere: **Stratosphere** &** Troposphere. **

**Explanation:__**

__
 
• About **90% of the ozone lies in the stratosphere region** and the rest **10% in the Troposphere**. So the** correct option will be Stratosphere**

**1. Stratospheric Ozone:**

 
• It is present in the upper atmosphere (typically extending from around **10 to 50 km **above the earth’s surface).
 
• **The concentrations of ozone are higher in the stratosphere****(about 90%)**. The stratosphere includes the zone termed the** ''ozone layer''.**
 
• In the stratosphere, ozone protects life on Earth from the sun’s ultraviolet radiation by absorbing a portion of the radiation from the sun and preventing it from reaching the planet's surface.
 
• Organisms on Earth are not adapted to heavy UV exposure, which kills or damages them. Without the ozone layer to reflect UVC and UVB radiation, most complex life on Earth would not survive long.

**2.** **Tropospheric Ozone:**

 
• It is the region of the atmosphere from the Earth’s surface and extends up to about **10 km.**
 
• **About 10% of the ozone is contained in the troposphere**. It is an important greenhouse gas and air pollutant, which is harmful to humans and other organisms. It is also a major component of urban smog.
 
• Tropospheric ozone is a short-lived climate pollutant with an atmospheric lifetime of hours to weeks.
 
• It does not have any direct emissions sources, rather it is a secondary gas formed by the interaction of sunlight with hydrocarbons, including methane and nitrogen oxides, which are emitted by vehicles, fossil fuel power plants, and other man-made sources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Atmospheric layer**
 **Characters**
 
 

 Thermosphere/Ionosphere
 
 
Temperature increases with height.

 
A thin layer called ionosphere is present in which energetic solar radiation knocks out electrons off molecules and atoms, turning them into "ions" with a positive charge.

 
 
 

 Exosphere
 
 
The outermost layer of the atmosphere.

 
It contains mainly oxygen and Hydrogen which are separated by a very large distance and due to which they never collide with each other.

questions.question: Which of the following organs is capable of removing unused or damaged platelets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**spleen.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **The thyroid **and **pancreas are primarily responsible for hormonal functions and digestion, respectively, and are not involved in blood cell removal.**
 
• Bone marrow produces platelets, not removes them.

 
• **The spleen, however, is known as the "graveyard of blood** cells" due to its **crucial role in filtering the blood and removing old, damaged, or unused red blood cells, as well as platelets.** It does this through macrophages, specialized cells that engulf and digest worn-out or defective cells. So, the correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question: Ascorbic acid is also known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin C.**__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Ascorbic acid** is also known as **Vitamin C.**
 
• It acts as an **antioxidant.**
 
• It is an essential nutrient for the body as it is involved in tissue repair and enzyme-related functions.
 
• A deficiency of vitamin C can cause a disease known as **scurvy.**
 
• Ascorbic acid or Vitamin C is primarily present in citrus fruits like **lemon, orange, guava.**
 
• It has a chemical formula - **C₆H₈O₆.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin A** is also known as **Retinol.**
 
• **Vitamin D** is also known as **Calciferol.**
 
• **Vitamin B **is complex comprising of different vitamins: **B1 (thiamine), B2 (riboflavin), B3 (niacin), B5 (pantothenic acid), B6 (pyridoxin), B7(biotin),B9 (folate) and B12 (cobalamin).**
